chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Playing tangos properly; Chick Webb the self-made drummer
summary: Webb insisted on correct tempos and slow rolls; McRae describes his self-made drive and ambition.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When we was in the Trianon, we go into these tangos. (Inaudible). I mean, we play tangos. We don't just be fooling with it, we play the right tempo.
Well the tango is South American. A lot of --
Yeah, but it's a certain way -- it's the right way to play a tango and it's a wrong way.

Oh yeah. We had a fella out there -- he'd be the first one on the floor. People would stand around and watch him, because he'd do that -- you know, with his heels and everything. And you don't play a tango -- it's got to be a tango tempo. And it's got to be authentic. You just can't get up there and play it because you're colored or you're a colored band playing the tango. No, you play the music! And this is what we used to do. We used to get waltzes. Like we'll play a Viennese waltz, be blast... (inaudible). The right tempo. See, tempo -- Chick say, "You're not a drummer if you can't play a slow and a beautiful thing." He'll tell you, he say, "Show me a guy to make me a slow roll," like tissue paper (inaudible). Slow roll. You're not a drummer unless you can do this. Chick Webb was a self-made drummer. In his life -- he tell in his story where he used to
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943

beat on the tin cans and things in Baltimore, and all that stuff. He was a self-made man. And he knew where he wanted to go. Way before I joined him. When I used to hang out with him, like I say before, (inaudible) he knew which direction where he wanted to go. He'd spend his last money. This is what he was going to do. He was going to do this, he was going to be here by this time, you know. Next year I want to be here and next year I want to be there. He told Charlie Buchanan, "Oh, you got a Caddy. I'm going to get one too." Two years later he had his Cadillac. The band was -- '37 -- the band was moving up. This was a great part about this man, you know. He was on his way.
Come back to that, but (inaudible) in Los Angeles now.
